text:
maria: Heads-up: support flagged tenant T-999 seeing mixed v1/v2 behavior in production graphs. Console says route pinned to v2 but downstream logs show v1 handler firing. Anyone familiar?
kevin: I glanced at the quota heatmap and saw spikes aligned with their peak. Thought it was request churn, but could be version mis-resolution.
jamie: Is this the route that uses route.meta.version with token-level opt-in? We had chosen route priority for that microservice.
sara: Yes, product insisted route takes precedence because clients don't always set the header. But the router should resolve to route when token_meta is missing.
maria: Example trace (short):
```
trace: c3f1a route:T-999/checkout header:X-Client-Version:v2 token_meta:expired resolved:legacy-handler kernel=v1-compat
```
kevin: Token cache TTL change last week might explain token_meta:expired. If the decision path treats an expired token_meta as "no-meta" and then falls back to legacy, that's wrong.
jamie: We need a clear policy: 1) if route.meta.version exists -> use that; 2) else if token_meta exists -> use token; 3) only fallback to legacy when both absent. Current code is doing (token first, then route).
sara: Agreed. I'll prepare a tiny patch to flip the order. Also we should be defensive: if token_meta is present but marked stale, don't prefer it over a fresh route meta.
maria: Telemetry-wise, ops asked why the console shows 100% v2 but customers see mixed. Root cause: console aggregates intended config (route meta) rather than resolved runtime decisions. UX mismatch.
kevin: Action items: emit a new routing field "resolved_version" in routing-decisions events and a low-cardinality "resolution_reason": {ROUTE, TOKEN, TOKEN_STALE, NONE}. That will make the graphs truthful.
jamie: For the console UX: add a "version reliability" sparkline per-tenant showing percent of requests resolved to route vs token over last 1h/24h. Hover tooltip shows explanation and link to raw decisions.
sara: Quota/billing impact: meters currently tag with incoming header and token header. We'll need to switch to tagging with resolved_version. That requires a small pipeline change in the meter emitter. Also reprocessing plan to backfill last 7 days if needed.
maria: Good. For the immediate mitigation, can we set auth-cache TTL to previous value as a hotfix to reduce token misses while we land the policy change?
kevin: Yes, we can rollback TTL for 2 hours. I'll schedule a short window.
jamie: Test plan: unit test for resolution precedence, integration test with simulated token expiry, and a canary rollout to 10% of traffic.
sara: I'll open PR INF-4902 with the policy change + telemetry field addition + migration note. Assign to @kevin for TTL rollback and @jamie for console mock.
ops-bot: New ticket INF-4902 created and linked to INF-4899 (tenant T-999 support).
maria: Timeline: TTL rollback in next 30m, policy patch + tests by EOD, telemetry emission in next deploy, console mock tomorrow morning.
kevin: Also propose a long-term: add a version-confidence metric (0-100) per route that combines recent resolved_version stability and token-cache health. That lets support quickly assess if a tenant truly switched.
jamie: I'll prototype the small badge in the console: green when confidence > 95, yellow 70-95, red <70. Include tooltip reasons.
sara: One more note: add an audit log entry when route.meta.version is changed so support isn't confused when someone flips route version.
maria: Solid. Thanks team 44d We'll sync at the 11am standup.
